system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Seller's "Key Negotiated Positions" and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)
**Basis:** Baseline deal – 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

---

## 0. Preliminary point: do not accept the framing

The Seller's preamble asserts that its positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams," "reflect the agreed commercial bargain," and are "marked FINAL and not intended to be re-opened." It also asserts that its liability package is "standard and widely accepted."

Treat this as advocacy, not record. Nothing in our instructions indicates any of these points were agreed at principal level, and a Seller's cover note is not evidence of a deal. Before responding, please confirm with the Wattlebridge principals whether *anything* in the liability package was actually agreed commercially. Absent confirmation, our mark-up should proceed on the basis that every position is open. Note also that the Disclosure Letter itself (para 11) says "No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included" – which contradicts the preamble's claim that the package is settled.

On the "market" claim: the figures cited are at the seller-friendly end of the range and, more importantly, the Seller's draft departs from market in ways the preamble does not mention (fundamental warranties capped with general warranties, knowledge qualification extending to "discoverable" matters, general data-room disclosure, limitations applying to *all* claims including fraud). Those are the real problems.

---

## 1. Liability regime (Clauses 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, 8.3)

### 1.1 General cap – 20% / AUD 4.8m
Low for a deal where (i) ~30% of revenue sits in one contract with an unresolved consent, (ii) there is a live privacy incident, (iii) IP ownership of SOW3 is unresolved, and (iv) a ~AUD 3.2m secured facility is undischarged. The cap should be set with those specific exposures in mind, and the matters in Section 2 below should be carved out and separately indemnified rather than absorbed within it.

**Recommendation:** Push for a materially higher general cap (open at 50%, settle no lower than ~30–35%), with specific indemnities (Section 2) and fundamental/tax/IP warranties sitting *outside* the cap.

### 1.2 De minimis and basket
AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 basket (~1.04%) with excess-only recovery. The de minimis is high for a business of this size – individual claims under AUD 25k (e.g. supplier overcharges, employee entitlements) will be numerous and collectively material.

**Recommendation:** De minimis AUD 10,000; basket AUD 120,000–150,000 (0.5–0.6%); **tipping** (first-dollar) basket rather than excess-only. Neither threshold should apply to fundamental warranties, tax, or specific indemnities.

### 1.3 Time limits – 18 months, and "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
18 months is short for a SaaS target with contingent privacy, IP and tax issues. The real problem is the second sentence: a default rule that *every* limitation applies to *every* claim means tax, title, capacity, fraud and the specific indemnities are all time-barred at 18 months unless we win an express carve-out for each one. That reverses the normal drafting burden.

**Recommendation:**
- General warranties: 24 months minimum.
- Tax warranties/indemnity: later of 7 years and the expiry of the relevant assessment period (ATO amendment periods make 18 months unworkable).
- Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority): 6 years (NSW limitation period) or uncapped in time.
- Specific indemnities: tied to the underlying exposure, not the general period.
- Delete the default sentence; replace with a rule that limitations apply only where expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / title warranties subject to general caps
This is the most significant departure in the liability package. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title to the shares fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing and the Seller's proposal would limit recovery to AUD 4.8m, net of basket, within 18 months.

**Recommendation:** Non-negotiable. Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no insolvency) capped at 100% of price (or uncapped), no basket/de minimis, 6-year or longer period.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
As drafted this purports to cap and time-bar claims for **fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment**, and also the specific indemnities and purchase-price adjustment claims. A limitation on liability for the Seller's own fraud is unlikely to be enforced but we should not be litigating enforceability. Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language also needs to preserve claims under the *Australian Consumer Law* s 18 (misleading or deceptive conduct) to the extent they cannot be excluded, and should be drafted to make clear the Buyer relies on the warranties and the Disclosure Letter.

**Recommendation:** Express carve-outs from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance for: fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct, wilful concealment; specific indemnities; completion accounts/price adjustment; and any liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.

### 1.6 Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)
The Seller excludes any claim for matters the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." Combined with general disclosure of the whole data room (Section 1.7), this would effectively convert the warranties into a representation that the data room is accurate, and nothing more. Constructive knowledge ("discoverable") is well beyond market. Imputed knowledge of "advisers" is also too wide.

**Recommendation:** Delete 8.3. If any knowledge qualification survives, confine it to **actual** knowledge of a short named list of deal-team individuals, and limit it to matters **fairly disclosed** (Section 1.7). Expressly exclude constructive/imputed knowledge and anything in public registers.

### 1.7 Disclosure – general data-room disclosure (Schedule 7; DL paras 1.1, 1.2)
The Disclosure Letter discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the entire data room, plus the accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." Paragraph 1.4 then disclaims that anything disclosed amounts to an admission that any consent, payment or remediation is required.

**Recommendation:**
- Disclosure must be **specific and fair**, i.e. disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely consequences. General data-room disclosure should be rejected or, at most, limited to documents specifically listed in an annexed index, and expressly excluding public registers.
- Delete the "publicly searchable corporate records" limb.
- Paragraph 1.4 should not operate to qualify the warranties – disclosure qualifies warranties; it cannot be both a disclosure and a denial that the matter matters.
- Disclosure should not be permitted against the fundamental warranties, the tax warranties, or the specific indemnities.
- We should run a **Buyer-side DD read-back**: each specific disclosure (paras 2–10) actually tells us something is *unresolved*. That is useful – it undermines the Seller's attempt to characterise those matters as "addressed" or "not material" in the SPA update.

---

## 2. Specific matters – the Disclosure Letter contradicts the SPA update

The pattern across items 2–10 is the same: the SPA update describes each matter as handled, immaterial or ordinary course; the Disclosure Letter (which the Seller will rely on to defeat warranty claims) concedes the opposite. We should use the Seller's own disclosures to justify conditions, price adjustments and indemnities.

### 2.1 Bluefen – ~AUD 3.6m revenue (~30%); consent **not obtained**
SPA update says the consent is "addressed" via reasonable endeavours and "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." Disclosure says there is no final written consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.

Problems: (a) "reasonable endeavours" is the weakest standard; (b) "treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent" leaves open conditional or qualified consent, consent subject to 11.3 conditions that are then not met, and consent from someone without authority; (c) 30% of revenue justifies a condition precedent.

**Recommendation:**
- Make Bluefen consent a **condition precedent** to Completion: unconditional written consent (or consent whose conditions are satisfied before Completion) from an authorised Bluefen signatory, in a form approved by the Buyer, with no amendment to pricing, term or termination rights.
- "Best endeavours" / "all reasonable endeavours" with a specified process and cost responsibility on the Seller.
- Walk right if not satisfied by the long-stop date.
- Fallback if the Seller will not accept a CP: price retention/escrow sized to the revenue at risk, plus a specific indemnity for loss of the Bluefen contract within 12–24 months post-Completion attributable to the change of control.

### 2.2 Riverlark Bank – ~AUD 3.2m facility; **release post-Completion**
This is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal. A post-Completion release means the Buyer acquires a company that is still secured borrower at Completion, with the Seller receiving the full price. There is also a change-of-control event at clause 8.1 of the facility that is itself a default trigger on Completion.

**Recommendation:**
- Repayment and **executed deed of release and discharge of all security (and PPSR discharge)** delivered **at Completion**, as a Completion deliverable, with the repayment amount deducted from the price via the funds flow (standard pay-off letter mechanics).
- Riverlark's change-of-control consent/waiver as a CP, or confirmation that the facility is repaid before the CoC event bites.
- Confirm there are no other facilities, guarantees, or security interests (PPSR search by Buyer).

### 2.3 DD-005 Completion bonuses – AUD 420,000, **not in funds flow**
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller." They are not: they are obligations of the *Company*, triggered by Completion, and will be paid by the Buyer's new subsidiary post-Completion. The Disclosure Letter also notes it is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs (typically ~15–20% on top).

**Recommendation:**
- Treat as a **Transaction Expense / debt-like item**: deduct the bonuses **plus** superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs from the price via the Completion funds flow, or have the Seller fund them directly at Completion.
- Confirm the continued-employment conditions do not create retention cliff risk for key people; consider whether we want retention arrangements of our own.
- Specific indemnity for any Completion-triggered employee payments not included in the funds flow.

### 2.4 Ironquay SOW3 – IP transfer conditional on payment; AUD 180,000 **open**
Clause 7.3 of the Ironquay contract conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. The Seller's own records show AUD 180,000 unpaid, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. The Seller's proposed indemnity is "limited to the SOW3 payment" – i.e. AUD 180k – which covers the fee but not the consequence (the Company may not own code in its product).

**Recommendation:**
- Pre-Completion: Seller to pay the AUD 180,000 and deliver a **confirmatory assignment / IP assignment deed** from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable (ideally a CP).
- Indemnity to extend to all loss arising from any defect in title to SOW1–3 materials, including third-party claims and cost of re-development/licensing, uncapped (or capped at price), outside the general regime.
- IP warranties: full ownership of all software, no third-party rights, all contractor IP validly assigned – not "settled under the general regime."

### 2.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident – ~1,240 records; **investigation preliminary**
The Seller calls it "a preliminary operational matter ... not expected to be material." The disclosure concedes it cannot say whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, what the scope is, or whether notification is required. That is the definition of an unresolved Notifiable Data Breach assessment under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth). The data (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) is personal information. Exposure includes OAIC regulatory action, customer contract breach (including possibly Bluefen/Mossvale), and penalties that have increased materially since 2022.

**Recommendation:**
- Pre-signing: Buyer to see the full incident file, the NDB assessment (if any), and correspondence with the unintended recipient.
- Seller to complete the assessment and, if required, notify OAIC and affected individuals **before Completion** (conduct of pre-Completion remediation to be approved by Buyer).
- Specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident, including regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and contract terminations – uncapped or capped at price, long period, not subject to basket/de minimis or disclosure.
- Privacy/data warranties to be given on a stand-alone basis.

### 2.6 Sandbar supplier renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000
The Seller describes these as ordinary-course. The Disclosure Letter says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – and tells us to read DD-008 and DD-011 "together for timing/scope." That is a hint that the three may be a single AUD 330k commitment split to look smaller, or may fall due around Completion.

**Recommendation:**
- DD follow-up: obtain the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, and whether any are prepaid or accrued at Completion.
- If they are committed and relate to pre-Completion periods or were accelerated into the sale window, treat as a working-capital/debt-like item in the completion accounts.
- Ensure the working-capital target and the accounts warranties capture them.

### 2.7 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Both disclosures are hedged: the lease has a "notification obligation" and Mossvale has an "assignment restriction" that the Seller says is not triggered "merely because shares are sold." We have not seen the clauses. Change-of-control clauses are frequently drafted as assignment restrictions and may be triggered by a share sale.

**Recommendation:** Review the actual clauses. If either is a CoC trigger, add to the consents CP list (Mossvale) or require landlord notice to be given pre-Completion (lease). Warranty that no contract contains a CoC right other than as listed in a schedule.

### 2.8 Title (DD-012)
Title is "evidenced by the Company share register." The Disclosure Letter itself notes that this is only the Seller's source and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.

**Recommendation:**
- Buyer to run ASIC company and PPSR searches, and review the share register, share certificates, constitution and any shareholder/option agreements.
- Full title and capacity warranties, uncapped, outside disclosure (see 1.4).
- Completion deliverables: original share certificates, executed transfers, board minutes approving registration, resignations, updated register.

### 2.9 Tax and IP warranties
"Settled under the general regime" is not acceptable for either.

**Recommendation:**
- **Tax:** full tax warranties plus a stand-alone **tax indemnity** for all pre-Completion tax, capped at price, 7-year period (or expiry of assessment period), no basket/de minimis, not qualified by disclosure except for specifically provided-for amounts.
- **IP:** stand-alone warranties on ownership, contractor assignments, open-source compliance, no infringement; longer period (e.g. 3–4 years); the Ironquay indemnity sits alongside.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "FINAL / agreed at principal level" | Asserted | Confirm with principals; treat as open unless confirmed |
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Open at 50%; settle ≥ 30–35%; specific indemnities and fundamental/tax/IP outside cap |
| 2 | De minimis / basket | 25k / 250k excess-only | 10k / 120–150k tipping; not applicable to fundamental, tax, indemnities |
| 3 | Time limits | 18 months, applies to all claims by default | 24m general; 7 yrs tax; 6 yrs fundamental; delete default rule |
| 4 | Fundamental/title warranties | Same as general | 100% cap or uncapped, no basket, 6+ years – non-negotiable |
| 5 | Limitations apply to "all Claims" | Includes fraud, indemnities | Carve out fraud/wilful concealment, specific indemnities, price adjustment, non-excludable statutory liability |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Actual + constructive + advisers | Delete; at most actual knowledge of named individuals of fairly disclosed matters |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers; 1.4 non-admission | Specific and fair disclosure only; delete public-register limb; no disclosure against fundamental/tax/indemnities |
| 8 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; consent not obtained | Unconditional consent as CP; walk right; fallback escrow + indemnity |
| 9 | Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) | Release post-Completion | Repay and discharge at Completion via funds flow; CoC waiver; PPSR discharge |
| 10 | Bonuses (AUD 420k) | Not in funds flow; "Seller matter" | Deduct from price with super/payroll tax/on-costs; indemnity |
| 11 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to AUD 180k | Pay + confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; broad IP indemnity |
| 12 | DD-006 privacy incident | "Not material" | Full incident file; NDB assessment pre-Completion; uncapped specific indemnity; stand-alone privacy warranties |
| 13 | Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | DD on contracts; treat as debt-like/working capital if accrued or accelerated |
| 14 | Lease / Mossvale | Not CoC | Review clauses; add to CP list if triggered |
| 15 | Title | Share register only | Buyer searches; uncapped title warranties |
| 16 | Tax / IP | "General regime" | Stand-alone tax indemnity (7 yrs); stand-alone IP warranties |

**Top priorities for the next call with the Seller:** (1) fundamental warranties outside the general regime; (2) Bluefen as a CP; (3) Riverlark discharge at Completion with price deduction; (4) bonuses and on-costs into the funds flow; (5) specific indemnities for DD-006 and Ironquay outside caps; (6) deletion of 8.3 and general data-room disclosure.

**Immediate DD actions for the Buyer team:** ASIC/PPSR searches; Bluefen clause 11.2/11.3 and consent correspondence; Riverlark facility clauses 8.1/9.2 and payout figure; DD-006 incident file; Ironquay SOW3 payment status (independent); Sandbar contracts; lease and Mossvale CoC clauses; employee bonus letters and on-cost calculation.

Happy to turn this into a formal mark-up of the SPA and a response to the Disclosure Letter once the principals confirm the status of the liability package.
=== END ADVICE ===
